name: tax identification number (TIN)
note: Qatar's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: natural persons without industrial, commercial, craft or professional activity are identified by their personal identification number (Qatari citizens) or residence permit number (foreign residents), whose length the sheet doesn't give; anyone with an activity or taxable income must apply to the General Tax Authority for a TIN: ten digits starting with 5 (Qatar's GCC code), nine generated by an algorithm including a check digit (rule not given, `check` left out). The TIN is kept here. Read as given on application, to anyone with taxable activity. No age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Qatar: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Natural persons who do not carry out industrial, commercial, craft or professional activities within the meaning of Article 1 of the Income Tax Law (ITL) are identified by their personal identification number (PIN), for Qatari citizens, and their residence permit number, for foreigners who are residents in Qatar. 1.2. Any Taxpayer who carries out an activity or derives a taxable income must register with the GTA and submit to the GTA an application for a tax identification number (TIN). ... The TIN consists of 10 digits. It begins with the number 5
